blocks.text: These are the glands that add fluids to sperms to form semen.

items: There are two seminal vesicles. Each of these glands releases a fluid rich in fructose (sugar) into the vas deferens through a duct. This fluid provides energy for the sperm.

The prostate gland lies just below the urinary bladder. It is soft and spongy and produces about 60% fluid of the semen. Semen is a mixture of sperms and fluids from the seminal vesicles and the prostate gland.
There are two small bulbourethral glands. They secrete a clear fluid that lubricates the urethra for sperm passage and provides a protective neutral environment for sperms to survive.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The figures for the two glands are swapped. The seminal vesicles produce the largest part of the semen, about 60% of its fluid; the prostate gland produces about 25–30%.
